Briefing · First edition

A briefing on the first edition: what it is, where and when it takes place, who it is for and how to take part. About seven minutes to read.

    V0.1.0 · 2026-10-06 · Draft

    In brief

    The Bienal in brief

    Bienal Blockchain Punta is an institutional platform for three groups that rarely share a table: the capital of the Southern Cone, the institutions that regulate it and the companies that build its financial infrastructure.

    The first edition takes place in Punta del Este, Uruguay, in March 2027, over two days and in two venues, MACA and Casa Manantial. The programme covers three subjects: stablecoins and payments, the tokenization of real assets, and the agentic economy. It is held every two years.

    I · The subject

    The agenda

    The 2027 edition is organised around one question — the opportunities and threats of a post-money world — and three subjects in which that question is already practical.

    Block01Stablecoins & PaymentsDollar stablecoins already carry a large share of the region’s digital-asset activity: in Argentina and Brazil they account for most of the crypto value received, above the global average. The open questions are institutional — who may issue, who settles, what backs the reserves and which rules apply across borders.
    Block02RWA & TokenizationTokenization moves the ownership of real assets — land, credit, receivables, fund units — onto shared ledgers. The block examines which assets move first, what legal certainty they need and how liquidity is created without weakening investor protection.
    Block03Agentic EconomySoftware agents are beginning to hold balances and make payments. The Bienal treats this as a question of capital and infrastructure rather than of product: how agentic payments are authorised, recorded and supervised, and who carries the liability.

    Source · Chainalysis, The 2024 Geography of Cryptocurrency Report · stablecoin share of value received

    I · The subject

    What it is, what it is not

    Five statements fix the format. Each one also rules something out.

    1. 01A biennial, not an annual summit.Editions in 2027, 2029 and 2031. Two years between editions gives regulation, products and capital positions time to move, so each edition measures change rather than repeating itself.
    2. 02Institutional, not experimental.The programme is built to a standard that the Central Bank of Uruguay and the Ministry of Economy and Finance could co-sign.
    3. 03A destination, not a venue.MACA, Casa Manantial and the city are part of the programme, not logistics around it.
    4. 04Art is periphery.The setting gives the Bienal weight. It does not set the agenda.
    5. 05AI enters through the capital door.Agentic payments and infrastructure, not product launches. The Bienal complements Punta Tech; it does not compete with it.

    II · The destination

    Why here, why now

    01Regulation in forceLaw 20,345 establishes Uruguay’s framework for virtual assets, and the Central Bank supervises their providers. Participants meet in a jurisdiction where the perimeter is written, not proposed.
    02Capital in seasonFamily offices and private capital from Argentina, Brazil and Uruguay spend the southern summer in Punta del Este. The Bienal meets them in March, where they already are.
    03Stable institutionsPredictable rules, and contracts denominated in US dollars as standard practice. For a central bank, a ministry or a bank, the location lowers the cost of taking part.
    04The destinationPunta del Este already carries weight in the region’s capital circles. Convening there says something before the programme begins.
    1.5trillion USDCrypto transaction volume in Latin America, July 2022 – June 2025.
    87.7billion USDThe region’s record month, December 2024.
    20,345LawUruguay’s virtual-asset law, in force.

    II · The destination

    Two venues, two layers

    The Bienal runs on two layers. The institutional layer is public and on the record. The private layer is where the same participants continue the conversation without an audience.

    Institutional layer · Forum and SummitMACAThe Museo de Arte Contemporáneo Atchugarry hosts the Forum and the Summit: the institutional layer, public and on the record. The next plate presents the building.
    Private layer · Dinner and PartyCasa ManantialCasa Manantial, co-producer of the Bienal, hosts the Dinner and the Party. Both are by invitation and off the record.

    The Forum and the Summit sit inside a working museum, not a convention hall.

    The Museo de Arte Contemporáneo Atchugarry opened in January 2022 in Manantiales, east of Punta del Este. Founded by the sculptor Pablo Atchugarry and designed by the architect Carlos Ott, it is open to the public year-round with an international exhibition programme. Holding the Bienal there sets the register before a word is spoken.

    • 2022Opened, 8 January
    • 5,000 m²Two connected buildings
    • 40 haGrounds, with a sculpture park of 70 artists

    III · The format

    Two days, five rooms

    Each room has one purpose and a planned size. None has an exhibition floor.

    III · The format

    Every two years

    The Bienal is a series. The format, the two venues and the three groups stay constant; the subject in the name can change between editions without a new brand. Two years is long enough for regulation, products and capital positions to move, and short enough to measure the change.

    Each edition is numbered · 2027 is Nº 001

    III · The format

    Three partners, three houses

    The Master and the two Diamond partners each hold a private villa for the weekend of the Bienal.

    /01 · The houseStaffed, private, co-brandedA villa in Punta del Este from Friday to Sunday, co-branded with the partner. Held within the Master and Diamond positions; not sold separately.
    /02 · The useThe partner’s own programmeTeam base, client meetings and a side programme with the partner’s own guest list. The partner may sell access to it and keeps the content it produces.
    /03 · The scheduleFixed slotsSide programmes run on Friday after the Dinner, on Saturday evening and on Sunday. They do not overlap the Forum or the Summit.

    IV · The people

    How to take part

    In short: capital, regulators and infrastructure at one table in Punta del Este, every two years from March 2027. Three subjects, two days, two venues. How to take part depends on which of the three groups you represent.

    /01 · CapitalAttend the Forum and the Summit, take part in the capital session, or join the edition as a partner.
    /02 · RulesSpeak on the record at the Forum, convene a closed roundtable, or support the edition institutionally.
    /03 · InfrastructurePresent a working system at the Summit, join a panel in one of the three blocks, or join the edition as a partner.
